headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage from Prefect's broad network egress; the cheatsheet agent is local-only and documentation-only, limiting pairwise blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between Prefect and python-cheatsheet: Prefect has broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Prefect output into python-cheatsheet prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or message bus.
Do not pipe Prefect output directly into python-cheatsheet prompts.
Add provenance tags before any manual copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: enforce channel allowlists in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, so it can transmit data off-host by default. python-cheatsheet is local-only and touches no data classes, so the pairwise leakage risk is driven by Prefect alone; uncertainty about any hidden shared workspace pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Prefect is given sensitive workflow metadata, that data can leave the host via network egress.
IF an operator later adds shared files containing secrets, leakage scope increases.
mitigations: Restrict Prefect to non-sensitive workflow metadata.
Block outbound traffic except approved endpoints.
Run python-cheatsheet in a separate workspace with no shared files.
Review Prefect logs for accidental metadata exposure.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress proxy controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect has network egress but no filesystem-write or git-modification capability is listed, while python-cheatsheet explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Prefect is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as another agent, conflict risk changes.
IF python-cheatsheet gains write capabilities, overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep write-capable tools off the shared workspace.
Do not grant git or filesystem write permissions to python-cheatsheet.
Separate any mutable resources by directory or account.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no action-taking surfaces, so it is unlikely to blindly execute Prefect output. Prefect can emit workflow metadata, but there is no evidence that python-cheatsheet treats it as authoritative; the cascade is therefore limited and requires an external orchestration step.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds Prefect output into python-cheatsheet as authoritative text, cascading errors become possible.
IF python-cheatsheet is repurposed to generate downstream actions, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any downstream action.
Label Prefect output as untrusted input.
Keep python-cheatsheet in documentation-only mode.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Prefect outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no secrets handled and no residency or retention mismatch documented. Prefect's broad network egress is the only compliance-relevant surface, but without a sensitive data class or jurisdictional constraint, the pairwise compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Prefect workflows, residency and retention controls must be rechecked.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdictional policy not reflected in the profiles, compliance risk may rise.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through Prefect.
Document retention settings for any workflow metadata.
Confirm deployment region before enabling network egress.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention.
